dossier.purpose: LlamaIndex OSS is a Python 'data framework' for building LLM, RAG and agent applications. Readers load documents (SimpleDirectoryReader plus 149 reader packages). An IngestionPipeline (transformations, cache, docstore hash dedup/upsert) chunks and embeds them into indices or vector stores. Retrievers and query engines answer over them. Agents and a workflow runtime are included. It is a monorepo: llama-index-core plus 551 separately published integration packages (LLMs, embeddings, vector stores, readers, tools, retrievers and more). README.md:11-15 says the company's primary focus has shifted to the hosted LlamaParse platform, LiteParse and benchmarks, while the OSS framework stays available. It is a library: no search server, CLI or MCP server for local document collections ships in this checkout, and no single tool converts all difficult-layout formats. Converters are separate optional reader packages (see code.architecture).

claims.claim: Current focus is 'the best AI-powered engine for document parsing and extraction'. LlamaParse is the enterprise platform for agentic OCR, parsing, extraction and indexing. LiteParse is a free, fast, cheap text parser. ParseBench and ExtractBench are open benchmarks.
'While we still have the OSS framework available as an open toolkit... our primary focus has shifted towards LlamaParse, along with liteparse and our benchmarking efforts.'
LlamaIndex OSS is an open-source framework to build agentic applications; LlamaParse can be used with it or on its own.
Two ways to start: the `llama-index` starter (core plus a selection of integrations) or `llama-index-core` plus chosen integration packages ('over 300' integration packages).
LlamaParse (hosted platform): Parse = 'Agentic OCR and document parsing (130+ formats)'; sign-up creates an account and API key; also Extract, Index, Split, Agents.
Data connectors ingest existing data sources and formats (APIs, PDFs, docs, SQL, etc.); indices/graphs structure the data; a retrieval/query interface returns retrieved context and augmented output.
Beginners can ingest and query data in 5 lines of code; lower-level APIs let advanced users customise data connectors, indices, retrievers, query engines and reranking modules.
Example: SimpleDirectoryReader(dir).load_data() then VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents) using OpenAI (OPENAI_API_KEY); alternative example with an Ollama LLM and HuggingFace embeddings.
By default data is stored in memory; index.storage_context.persist() writes under ./storage; reload with StorageContext.from_defaults(persist_dir=...) and load_index_from_storage.

llama-index-core ships a `_static` folder with nltk and tiktoken caches so it runs where runtime disk access is restricted; the GitHub attest-build-provenance action attests those files and `gh attestation verify` can check them.
New integrations should integrate meaningfully with core; maintainers may decline some.
README is not updated as frequently as the documentation; docs are hosted at developers.llamaindex.ai.
Examples are in docs/examples; 'Indices are in the `indices` folder (see list of indices below)'.

install.command: pip install llama-index-core; pip install llama-index-llms-openai; pip install llama-index-llms-ollama; pip install llama-index-embeddings-huggingface
pip install llama-index-core llama-index-readers-file llama-index-llms-ollama llama-index-embeddings-huggingface
git clone https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index.git; pip install -e llama-index-core   (docs precede this with `poetry shell`; CONTRIBUTING.md:15-20 uses `uv sync` instead)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - CI runs build, lint, typecheck and unit tests on Ubuntu runners (.github/workflows/unit_test.yml:12, build_package.yml:16, lint.yml:11). The CPU architecture is not stated in the repo. llama-index-core is built with hatchling from Python sources (llama-index-core/pyproject.toml:109-125); compiled dependencies such as numpy and tiktoken come from PyPI.
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL2 statement in README or framework docs (the only WSL mention is a Celery-on-Windows aside, docs/src/content/docs/framework/understanding/putting_it_all_together/apps/fullstack_with_delphic.md:43) and no WSL CI job.
platforms.macos_arm64: unknown - no macOS support statement and no macOS CI job (build matrix is ubuntu-latest + windows-latest, .github/workflows/build_package.yml:16; unit tests are Ubuntu only, unit_test.yml:12). Docs show macOS/Linux shell syntax (docs/src/content/docs/framework/getting_started/starter_example.mdx:25-26), note Linux/macOS multiprocessing behaviour (docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/loading/simpledirectoryreader.md:37-42), and core can select the Apple 'mps' torch device (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/utils.py:593-594).
platforms.gpu: yes (optional, integration-specific) - llama-index-core has no torch/GPU dependency (llama-index-core/pyproject.toml:57-87) and only picks cuda/mps/cpu when a local torch model is used (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/utils.py:583-595). GPU use lives in optional packages, e.g. LayoutIR use_gpu (llama-index-integrations/readers/llama-index-readers-layoutir/README.md:54-63), the marker reader's VRAM note (llama-index-integrations/readers/llama-index-readers-pdf-marker/llama_index/readers/pdf_marker/base.py:33) and the Donut image reader (llama-index-integrations/readers/llama-index-readers-file/llama_index/readers/file/image/base.py:108).

integrations.cli: None for search, ingest or readback in this checkout. The old `llamaindex-cli` RAG CLI moved to a separate `llama-index-cli` package: llama-index-core/llama_index/core/command_line/__init__.py:1 says 'Deprecated. CLI is now its own package llama-index-cli'. No llama-index-cli/ directory exists at v0.14.25 and the starter does not depend on it (pyproject.toml:41-46), although SECURITY.md:14 and CONTRIBUTING.md:66 still name it. The only CLI shipped from this repo is `llama-dev` (monorepo package/test/release tooling: llama-dev/pyproject.toml:28-29, llama-dev/llama_dev/cli.py:24-44).
integrations.mcp: Client side only in this repo. `llama-index-tools-mcp` provides BasicMCPClient, McpToolSpec and get_tools_from_mcp_url so agents can call tools of existing MCP servers (llama-index-integrations/tools/llama-index-tools-mcp/README.md:3, llama_index/tools/mcp/__init__.py:1-15; depends on mcp>=2.0.0,<3 at pyproject.toml:44). The helper `workflow_as_mcp(workflow, ...)` wraps a user-written Workflow as an `MCPServer` (llama_index/tools/mcp/utils.py:77-141; README.md:58-101). It is not a ready-made document-search server, and the bundled example server is an IP-info demo (examples/mcp_server.py:27-54). Docs point to a separate `llamacloud-mcp` server (a different repo, not in this checkout) that queries LlamaCloud indexes and LlamaExtract agents and needs a LlamaCloud org, project and API key (docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/mcp/llamacloud_mcp.md:5-9, 17-52).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Python SDK: llama-index-core plus integration packages, imported as llama_index.core.* or llama_index.<kind>.<name> (README.md:35-49). Relevant classes are SimpleDirectoryReader, IngestionPipeline, VectorStoreIndex/VectorIndexRetriever, BM25Retriever and QueryFusionRetriever (see code.entry_points). No HTTP API or server ships in the repo. The hosted LlamaCloud API (https://api.cloud.llamaindex.ai, llama-index-core/llama_index/core/constants.py:35-36) is a separate service, and core's LlamaCloud client helpers are marked deprecated and never called (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/ingestion/api_utils.py:14-49).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: No Claude Code plugin/skill/hook, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or Codex integration found (searched repo-wide for 'claude code', 'codex', CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md; the only other hit is a gitignore entry at llama-index-integrations/readers/llama-index-readers-layoutir/.gitignore:155-157). The sole mention: docs show adding the external `llamacloud-mcp` server to the config of 'an MCP host like claude-code' (docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/mcp/llamacloud_mcp.md:19-52, with the API key passed in args at :38-39). No Codex mention.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or phone-home code found in llama-index-core (searched telemetry, posthog, sentry, analytics, mixpanel, opt-out; only unrelated names in llama-index-core/llama_index/core/command_line/mappings.json). Observability is opt-in: set_global_handler() can enable third-party handlers (wandb, openinference, arize_phoenix, honeyhive, promptlayer, deepeval, simple, argilla, langfuse, agentops, literalai, opik; llama-index-core/llama_index/core/callbacks/global_handlers.py:6-147); the default global_handler is None (llama_index/core/__init__.py:145) and the instrumentation dispatcher defaults to Null handlers (llama-index-instrumentation/src/llama_index_instrumentation/__init__.py:13-18). Accounts and network: the default LLM and embedding model resolve to OpenAI and raise unless OPENAI_API_KEY is valid (llama_index/core/llms/utils.py:40-71, llama_index/core/embeddings/utils.py:42-76; docs/src/content/docs/framework/getting_started/installation.mdx:30-33). Env IS_TESTING swaps in mocks (llms/utils.py:42-47). A local alternative (Ollama plus HuggingFace embeddings) is documented (README.md:138-164; docs/.../getting_started/starter_example_local.mdx:26-30, 128-147). Runtime downloads: NLTK stopwords/punkt_tab are bundled in `_static` of the released package and fetched with nltk.download only if the bundled cache is missing (llama_index/core/utils.py:56-70, 83-102; installation.mdx:28); tiktoken uses the bundled cache dir unless TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR is set (utils.py:165-179). In a git checkout `_static` holds only .gitignore placeholders (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/_static/.gitignore) because the caches are generated in release.yml:36-41. URL inputs are fetched with requests.get in resolve_binary (utils.py:626-710, 704), and SimpleDirectoryReader can read remote filesystems via fsspec (docs/.../loading/simpledirectoryreader.md:166-189). LlamaParse (hosted) needs a LlamaCloud account and API key (README.md:55; env LLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY, default API URL constants.py:35-36); the in-repo llama-parse reader is a deprecated wrapper (llama-index-integrations/readers/llama-index-readers-llama-parse/README.md:3). Other converter readers: the Upstage reader posts to https://api.upstage.ai and needs UPSTAGE_API_KEY (llama-index-readers-upstage/llama_index/readers/upstage/base.py:13, 145-171); DashScope parse needs an API key (llama-index-readers-dashscope/README.md:27-33); the Legacy Office reader downloads a Tika JAR on first use and runs a local server on port 9998 (llama-index-readers-legacy-office/README.md:63-64); Donut image OCR, when enabled, downloads naver-clova-ix/donut-base-finetuned-cord-v2 from Hugging Face (llama-index-readers-file/.../image/base.py:62-67); PPTX image captioning (off by default, slides/base.py:43) downloads nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning (slides/image_extractor.py:46-53). The Docling reader accepts URLs (llama-index-readers-docling/llama_index/readers/docling/base.py:56); whether Docling downloads models is not checkable from this repo.

entry_points.what: SimpleDirectoryReader (line 208): directory/file loader. Default PDF/DOCX/PPTX/EPUB/image/XLSX extractors come from llama-index-readers-file only if installed (68-113). Unmapped extensions (.md, .html, .txt) are read as raw text (634-644). Metadata includes file_path, file_name, file_type, file_size and dates (148-184). filename_as_id=True gives stable ids (628-643).

IngestionPipeline (262): transformations, IngestionCache, optional vector_store and docstore. DocstoreStrategy UPSERTS/DUPLICATES_ONLY/UPSERTS_AND_DELETE (242-259) based on doc-id/hash maps. run()/arun() store input documents in the docstore when store_doc_text=True (518-536, 539-662). persist()/load() default to ./pipeline_storage (374-421).

VectorIndexRetriever (24-80): vector_store_query_mode (VectorStoreQueryMode DEFAULT/SPARSE/HYBRID/TEXT_SEARCH/SEMANTIC_HYBRID/MMR, vector_stores/types.py:45-60), alpha, sparse_top_k, hybrid_top_k, metadata filters, doc_ids. Used by VectorStoreIndex (indices/vector_store/base.py).

QueryFusionRetriever (33): fuses several retrievers (e.g. vector plus BM25) with simple / reciprocal-rank / relative-score / dist-based fusion (24-30); num_queries defaults to 4, so it calls the LLM to generate extra queries unless num_queries=1 (41, 276-279).

BM25Retriever (41): lexical retriever over nodes using bm25s and PyStemmer; from_defaults(index|nodes|docstore), persist()/from_persist_dir() (211-227), metadata-filter weight mask. Separate PyPI package; its README is a single heading line.

DoclingReader (15): wraps docling DocumentConverter; exports each source (file path or URL) to Markdown or Docling-JSON text as one Document with a random uuid4 id by default (41-44, 46-83). Wrapper only; the conversion is done by the docling library.

`llama-dev` console script (llama-dev/pyproject.toml:28-29): click group with pkg, test and release subcommands for monorepo development. It is the only CLI shipped from this repo. (llama-index-instrumentation/pyproject.toml:18-19 declares a `llama-index-instrumentation` script pointing at llama_index_instrumentation:main, but no `main` exists in that package.)
workflow_as_mcp (77-141) returns an MCPServer exposing a Workflow as one tool; get_tools_from_mcp_url/aget_tools_from_mcp_url (20-74) are client-side. No server main.

code.architecture: Python monorepo (hatchling build, uv workflows) of independently versioned packages. (1) llama-index-core/llama_index/core/ is the framework: readers/ (BaseReader; readers/file/base.py SimpleDirectoryReader), ingestion/ (pipeline.py, cache.py), node_parser/ (SentenceSplitter, file/markdown.py MarkdownNodeParser, HTML/JSON parsers, relational/ element parsers incl. markdown_element.py and llama_parse_json_element.py that summarise tables with an LLM via base_element.py:194-236), schema.py (Document, TextNode, NodeRelationship.SOURCE, sha256 hash), indices/ (vector_store, keyword_table incl. Simple/RAKE variants, summary, tree, knowledge graph, property graph), retrievers/ (fusion, auto_merging, recursive, router, transform), vector_stores/ (types.py VectorStoreQueryMode; simple.py in-memory store), storage/ (StorageContext, docstore, index_store, kvstore; default persist dir ./storage), plus embeddings/, llms/, query_engine/, chat_engine/, agent/, tools/, memory/, evaluation/ and callbacks/. instrumentation/ and workflow/ are thin re-exports of the separately published llama-index-instrumentation and `workflows` (llama-index-workflows) packages (llama-index-core/pyproject.toml:83; llama-index-core/uv.lock:1590-1597). (2) llama-index-integrations/<kind>/<package>/ holds 551 separately published packages (e.g. 149 under readers/, plus llms, embeddings, vector_stores, tools, retrievers, node_parser, graph_stores, callbacks, indices, ingestion, agent, extractors, graph_rag), each with its own pyproject.toml, uv.lock and tests/. (3) The root pyproject.toml is the `llama-index` starter meta-package (dependencies only; its hatch include path _llama-index/llama_index is absent from the checkout). (4) llama-index-instrumentation/ (dispatcher/event/span observability), llama-index-utils/ (4 packages), llama-dev/ (monorepo CLI), docs/ (framework docs, API reference, examples). llama-index-cli, llama-index-packs, llama-index-experimental and llama-index-finetuning are absent from this checkout although CONTRIBUTING.md:61-66, SECURITY.md:14 and Makefile:22-29 still reference them. Document path: SimpleDirectoryReader -> Document -> IngestionPipeline (transformations plus optional vector_store and docstore) -> TextNodes with a SOURCE relationship to the parent document and best-effort char offsets (node_parser/node_utils.py:42, node_parser/interface.py:104-118) -> vector store and/or docstore -> retrievers. Document-conversion options in the repo (none is a single all-format tool; each is a separately installed wrapper): llama-index-readers-file defaults (PDF via pypdf plain text per page, docs/base.py:79-98; DOCX via docx2txt text, docs/base.py:126-133; PPTX via python-pptx; EPUB via EbookLib+html2text, epub/base.py:51-56; images with OCR off by default, image/base.py:31; PyMuPDFReader plain text; UnstructuredReader via local `unstructured` or the Unstructured API, unstructured/base.py:124-152; HTML only via HTMLTagReader <section> text, html/base.py:11-77, not in the default map); llama-index-readers-docling (PDF, DOCX, HTML and 'other document types' to Markdown or Docling JSON; README.md:5, base.py:72-77; JSON export needs the Docling node parser, README.md:43-45); llama-index-readers-markitdown (MarkItDown 0.1.0 to Markdown for .docx .html .xml .csv .pdf .pptx .xlsx .json .zip .txt .md; no .epub or image types in its allow-list, markitdown/base.py:53-66; ignores extra_info, 109-129); llama-index-readers-pdf-marker (PDF to Markdown with OCR languages, marker-pdf>=0.2.0,<0.3, GPL-3.0-or-later); llama-index-readers-nougat-ocr (PDF to Markdown via the nougat CLI, GPL-2.0-or-later); llama-index-readers-paddle-ocr (PDF text plus OCR of embedded images); llama-index-readers-layoutir (PDF layout blocks, Python>=3.12); llama-index-readers-legacy-office (.doc via a local Apache Tika server, Java 11+); cloud: LlamaParse via the deprecated llama-index-readers-llama-parse wrapper (account/API key), Upstage Document Parse (text/html output, API key, AGPL-3.0), DashScope.
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: sdists and wheels built with `uv build` (hatchling) and published to PyPI for llama-index-core and the llama-index starter (both 0.14.25; requires-python >=3.10,<4.0; llama-index-core/pyproject.toml:37-40, pyproject.toml:68-69) and for each sub-package. .github/workflows/release.yml runs on workflow_dispatch or when the release PR from vars.RELEASE_BRANCH_NAME is merged into main (3-9, 18): it populates the nltk/tiktoken caches (36-41), runs actions/attest-build-provenance@v4 over llama-index-core/llama_index/core/_static/**/* (43-47), runs core tests (49-52), then `uv publish --token ${{ secrets.LLAMA_INDEX_PYPI_TOKEN }}` (54-59, 116-120). The GitHub Release v<version> attaches only dist/*.tar.gz built at the repo root, i.e. the starter meta-package sdist (105-137). publish_sub_package.yml publishes any sub-package whose version is missing from PyPI on every push to main with `uv publish --token` and no test step (67-124). pre_release.yml opens the release PR using `llama-dev release prepare/changelog` (39-62). No checksums, signatures or attestations are produced for the wheels/sdists; the only attestation covers the `_static` cache files (README.md:191-208 documents verifying them with `gh attestation verify`). The cache directories are .gitignore placeholders in git and are generated at release time. sync-docs.yml copies docs to the run-llama/developers repo (sync-docs.yml:33-38, 49-63).
code.tests_and_ci: pytest (+pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, pytest-timeout, pytest-mock; llama-index-core/pyproject.toml:5-33). Test dirs: llama-index-core/tests/ (192 test_*.py files; 256 .py including conftest/helpers), llama-index-integrations/**/tests/ (737 test_*.py across 551 packages), llama-index-instrumentation/tests/ (4), llama-dev/tests/ (8): roughly 940 test files. CONTRIBUTING.md:104-110 asks contributors to mock remote systems and states CI fails below 50% coverage. 14 workflows in .github/workflows: unit_test.yml (pull_request only; `llama-dev test --base-ref` runs pytest in changed packages and their dependants on Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 on ubuntu-latest-unit-tester, plus llama-index-core with coverage on 3.14: lines 3-4, 12-16, 44-71); coverage_check.yml (PR; diff-cover >=50% on changed lines, Python 3.12: lines 6-10, 35-46); build_package.yml (push to main and PR; uv build, install the wheel, import llama_index on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest); lint.yml (pre-commit: ruff, ruff-format, mypy, black/blacken-docs, prettier, codespell, nb-clean, toml-sort, detect-private-key; .pre-commit-config.yaml); core-typecheck.yml (mypy on llama-index-core, Python 3.12); codeql.yml (python; push, PR and weekly cron); llama_dev_tests.yml (pytest for llama-dev when it changes); release.yml, pre_release.yml, publish_sub_package.yml (release); sync-docs.yml (docs sync); close_new_integration_prs.yml, stale_bot.yml, issue_classifier.yml (repo hygiene; the classifier uses a LlamaCloud API key secret, issue_classifier.yml:24); dependabot.yml (weekly github-actions and uv updates). llama-dev test skips packages without tests or with incompatible Python, does not fail CI when a package fails to install, and reports a 300 s pytest timeout as 'no tests' (llama-dev/llama_dev/test/__init__.py:360-365, 538-548). The Makefile still lists pants-based test targets (Makefile:13-29) that CI does not use. Reader-wrapper tests are thin: docling has 2 mocked tests (readers-docling/tests/test_readers_docling.py:92-140), markitdown has 1 class test (tests/test_markitdownreader.py:5), pdf-marker has no tests directory.

Examples: readers-file 6 (beautifulsoup4, pypdf, striprtf, pandas, llama-index-core, defusedxml; optional pymupdf extra, pyproject.toml:72-82); readers-docling 4 (llama-index-core, docling-core, docling, numpy>=2.0); readers-markitdown 2 (markitdown[all]==0.1.0, llama-index-core); readers-llama-parse 2 (llama-parse>=0.5.0, llama-index-core); readers-pdf-marker 2 (marker-pdf>=0.2.0,<0.3, llama-index-core); retrievers-bm25 3 (bm25s, pystemmer, llama-index-core); tools-mcp 3 (mcp>=2.0.0,<3, llama-index-core, pydantic). docs/api_reference/pyproject.toml is a Poetry manifest for the docs build only.
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md (repo root). Huntr bug bounty covers only llama-index, llama-index-core, llama-index-embeddings-openai, llama-index-llms-openai and llama-index-cli (SECURITY.md:5-14); other integrations are out of scope but reportable via GitHub's private 'Report a vulnerability' form (16-28); LlamaCloud issues and other concerns go to security@llamaindex.ai (70-80). Threat model: a library for trusted execution environments; input validation, authN/Z and rate limiting belong to the host application (30-38). Out-of-scope classes: SSRF via loaders/helpers (resolve_image, download_loader, readers), path traversal/deserialization with untrusted paths, prompt injection, DoS from unbounded input, OWASP-style bugs in host handlers (40-48). In-scope examples: insecure temp files, secrets in debug logs, disabled TLS verification (52-68). Supporting controls: CodeQL (.github/workflows/codeql.yml), dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml), detect-private-key hook (.pre-commit-config.yaml:16).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:28 - `llama-index` is a starter package that includes core LlamaIndex plus a selection of integrations
claim_checks.evidence: Root pyproject.toml:41-46 lists only llama-index-core, llama-index-embeddings-openai, llama-index-llms-openai and nltk. docs/src/content/docs/framework/getting_started/installation.mdx:21-26 also lists llama-index-readers-file in the bundle, but the manifest does not depend on it (code wins). So `pip install llama-index` does not install the default PDF/DOCX/PPTX/EPUB readers (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/readers/file/base.py:68-90).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:89 - data connectors ingest existing data sources and formats (APIs, PDFs, docs, SQL, etc.)
claim_checks.evidence: Connectors are separate packages (149 under llama-index-integrations/readers). SimpleDirectoryReader's default PDF/DOCX/PPTX/EPUB/image/XLSX readers come from llama-index-readers-file and are used only if it is installed. Otherwise a warning is logged and the file is decoded as UTF-8 text with errors ignored (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/readers/file/base.py:68-113, 634-644). Even with it installed, DOCX/EPUB/PPTX/XLSX/HWP readers import packages it does not declare: docx2txt (readers/file/docs/base.py:117), ebooklib+html2text (epub/base.py:29-31), pptx (slides/base.py:342), openpyxl (tabular/base.py:189), olefile (docs/base.py:165); declared deps are at llama-index-readers-file/pyproject.toml:72-79. An ImportError aborts the whole load (core readers/file/base.py:614-617). PDF output is plain text from pypdf (docs/base.py:79-98) and DOCX output is docx2txt text (docs/base.py:126-133), not Markdown.

The default extractor map in code (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/readers/file/base.py:92-112) has no .md (nor .html/.txt) entry, so those files fall through to a raw-text read (634-644): the full original text is kept as Document.text but nothing parses Markdown or HTML. risks: Maintenance focus and stale directories: README.md:11-15 says the primary focus moved to hosted LlamaParse/LiteParse/benchmarks. CONTRIBUTING.md:59-66 stops accepting new integration packages and discourages CLI/packs/finetuning/experimental work. STALE.md:5, 32-46 lets low-health integrations move to a stale_packages branch. Those CLI/packs/experimental/finetuning directories are absent from this checkout, yet SECURITY.md:14, CONTRIBUTING.md:61-66 and Makefile:22-29 (pants test targets) still reference them. The project is still actively released (CHANGELOG.md:5,55: llama-index-core 0.14.25, 2026-09-21).

No turnkey 'search a Markdown collection and read original bodies back' tool for any CLI agent: no CLI (llamaindex-cli moved to a package not in this repo, llama-index-core/llama_index/core/command_line/__init__.py:1); no MCP server for local documents (llama-index-tools-mcp is a client plus a `workflow_as_mcp` helper, llama-index-integrations/tools/llama-index-tools-mcp/README.md:3, llama_index/tools/mcp/utils.py:77-141); the documented llamacloud-mcp server is in another repo, serves LlamaCloud indexes and needs an account and API key (docs/src/content/docs/framework/module_guides/mcp/llamacloud_mcp.md:5-9, 38-39). Any Claude Code/Codex wiring means writing glue code; no Claude Code/Codex integration, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md ships.

Ingestion fidelity and silent-failure hazards: (a) the starter omits llama-index-readers-file (pyproject.toml:41-46), so PDFs/Office/EPUB are decoded as raw text bytes with errors ignored after only a logger warning (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/readers/file/base.py:85-90, 634-644); (b) with it installed, docx/epub/pptx/xlsx readers need undeclared extra packages and an ImportError aborts the whole load (llama-index-readers-file/pyproject.toml:72-79; core base.py:614-617); (c) other read errors print 'Skipping...' and drop the file unless raise_on_error=True (base.py:618-626); (d) scans/images yield empty text by default (ImageReader parse_text=False, llama-index-readers-file/.../image/base.py:31, 101-102); (e) wrapper behaviour varies: PDFPaddleOCRReader returns the exception text as a Document on failure (llama-index-readers-paddle-ocr/.../base.py:161-168), PDFNougatOCR returns None on failure and writes to a relative ./output dir (nougat_ocr/base.py:29-31, 53-54), PDFMarkerReader reloads all models on every call (pdf_marker/base.py:43); (f) MarkdownReader strips links/images/HTML/blank lines (markdown/base.py:56-59, 95-101), and MarkItDownReader ignores extra_info and has no .epub or image extensions in its allow-list (markitdown/base.py:53-66, 109-129).

Original-body readback and provenance are not automatic: VectorStoreIndex.from_documents stores only per-document hashes plus chunk nodes, not the full Document text (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/indices/base.py:111-129). Only IngestionPipeline with a docstore keeps the input documents (store_doc_text defaults True, ingestion/pipeline.py:518-536, 546, 655-660). When a vector store keeps text, the docstore gets no chunk text unless store_nodes_override=True (indices/vector_store/base.py:43, 234-250). Document ids default to random uuid4 (schema.py:275-277), so stable upserts need filename_as_id=True or explicit ids (readers/file/base.py:628-631), and UPSERTS silently falls back to duplicates_only when no vector store is attached (pipeline.py:574-588). Chunk start/end offsets are best-effort str.find() matches (node_parser/interface.py:104-118); the source link is a node relationship (node_parser/node_utils.py:42).

Search-mode caveats: the stock SimpleVectorStore supports only default, MMR and learner modes, and other modes (hybrid, sparse, text_search) raise ValueError (llama-index-core/llama_index/core/vector_stores/simple.py:35-41, 286-310). BM25 is a separate package with a one-line README (llama-index-retrievers-bm25/README.md:1, base.py:41-86). Hybrid needs a vector store implementing HYBRID/SPARSE or manual fusion, and QueryFusionRetriever defaults to num_queries=4, which makes an LLM call (default resolves to OpenAI) per query unless num_queries=1 (retrievers/fusion_retriever.py:41, 62-64, 276-279). Default similarity_top_k is 2 (constants.py:12). Default LLM and embeddings need OPENAI_API_KEY and network (llms/utils.py:40-71, embeddings/utils.py:42-76). MarkdownElementNodeParser and LlamaParseJsonNodeParser summarise tables with an LLM (node_parser/relational/base_element.py:194-236).

Licensing is not uniformly MIT. The top-level LICENSE and core are MIT (LICENSE:1; llama-index-core/pyproject.toml:42), but several in-repo packages declare copyleft licenses, including document converters: GPL-3.0-or-later for readers pdf-marker (pyproject.toml:36; its LICENSE file is the GPLv3 text), pdf-table (:34), web (:35), boarddocs, stripe-docs and service-now; GPL-2.0-or-later for readers nougat-ocr (:36); GPL-2.0-only for imdb-review; AGPL-3.0 for readers-upstage (:34, hard-depends on pymupdf at :36), llms-upstage, callbacks-uptrain and readers-kaltura. readers-file also offers an optional pymupdf extra (pyproject.toml:81-82). Licenses of third-party converters (Docling, MarkItDown, marker, PyMuPDF) are not stated in this repo and were not checked.

Release and CI assurance gaps: PyPI publishing uses a long-lived token secret (.github/workflows/release.yml:59, 120; publish_sub_package.yml:115). The only provenance attestation covers llama-index-core's `_static` cache files (release.yml:43-47); there are no checksums/signatures/attestations for sdists or wheels, and the GitHub Release attaches only the root starter's sdist (release.yml:130-137). Sub-package publishing on push to main has no test step (publish_sub_package.yml:67-124). llama-dev test does not fail CI on install failures and treats a 300 s pytest timeout as 'no tests' (llama-dev/llama_dev/test/__init__.py:360-365, 538-548). Unit tests run only on pull requests and only on Linux, with no macOS job (unit_test.yml:3-4, 12). Reader-wrapper tests are thin (docling 2 mocked tests, markitdown 1 class test, pdf-marker none). Converter pins are narrow or old: marker-pdf>=0.2.0,<0.3 (pdf-marker/pyproject.toml:38), markitdown[all]==0.1.0 (markitdown/pyproject.toml:37), and the LayoutIR reader needs Python>=3.12 versus core's >=3.10 (layoutir/pyproject.toml:34).

Security model leaves untrusted-input handling to the host app: SECURITY.md:32-48 puts SSRF via loaders/helpers, path traversal or deserialization from untrusted paths, prompt injection and unbounded-input DoS out of scope. SimpleDirectoryReader reads every non-hidden file it finds as text by default (required_exts=None, llama-index-core/llama_index/core/readers/file/base.py:249-266; docs/.../simpledirectoryreader.md:9), and resolve_binary fetches arbitrary URLs with requests.get (llama_index/core/utils.py:626-710, 704). SECURITY.md:5-14 limits the bounty to llama-index, core, the OpenAI LLM/embeddings packages and llama-index-cli, which is not in this repo.
